full_judgment:
“To prove the charge, it has to be proved beyond reasonable doubt that the accused voluntarily accepted money knowing it to be bribe. The absence of proof of demand for illegal gratification and mere possession or recovery of currency notes is not sufficient to constitute such offence. In the said judgments it is also held that even the presumption under Section 20 of the Act can be drawn only after demand for and acceptance of illegal gratification is proved. It is also fairly well settled that initial presumption of innocence in the criminal jurisprudence gets doubled by acquittal recorded by the trial court.” Thus, the demand for gratification and its acceptance must be proved beyond a reasonable doubt.” 

 “Proof of demand of illegal gratification is gravamen for offences punishable under Sections 7 and 13(1)(d)(i) and (ii) of the Act, 1988. Mere acceptance of any amount by way of gratification or recovery thereof dehors the proof of demand would not be sufficient to bring home the charge under aforesaid sections of the Act, 1988. The proof of demand is a sine qua non and in the absence of proof of demand, legal presumption under Section 20 of the Act, 1988, cannot be raised.”
